device.name: Matterix Test Beakers Franka (Isaac Lab simulation)

facts.text: Matterix describes itself as a multi-scale, GPU-accelerated robotic simulation framework for digital twins of chemistry labs
The documented setup installs isaaclab[isaacsim,all]==3.0.0b2.post1, so Isaac Sim and Isaac Lab are external dependencies of the simulator stack
The project builds the environment configuration with parse_env_cfg and then calls gym.make(task, cfg=env_cfg), so a bare gym.make(env_id) has no cfg
MatterixBaseEnv derives from ManagerBasedEnv and gym.Env
The environment is vectorized: is_vector_env is True

step applies the action, advances cfg.decimation physics steps, updates the semantic manager, computes terminations and rewards, resets terminated environments and returns observations, rewards, terminated, truncated and extras
reset accepts seed, env_ids and options, sets the seed when given, resets the requested environments and returns the observations and extras

The observation space is a gym.spaces.Dict of Box spaces with infinite bounds built from the observation terms, the action space is Box(low=-inf, high=inf, shape=(action_dim,)), and both are batched for num_envs
The maximum episode length is ceil(episode_length_s / step_dt) environment steps
The default control decimation is 5 action updates per policy step
The default physics timestep is 1/60 s
Matterix-Test-Beakers-Franka-v1 is registered with entry point matterix.envs:MatterixBaseEnv
The Beakers test task declares a non-concatenated policy observation group with the terms ee_pos_robot and ee_pos_robot2, both computed by mdp.ee_env_pos
ee_env_pos returns the end-effector position in the environment frame as three coordinates
The Beakers test task configures two Franka arms, robot (joint position control) and robot2 (differential IK control)

determinism.notes: reset(seed) sets the Isaac Lab seed before the scene reset (matterix_base_env.py:531-533), so a seeded run repeats on the same installation; the fake uses Python's random.Random and was never compared with the upstream environment, and no exact bit-for-bit claim is made

gaps: the fake backend is a kinematic stand-in: it integrates a placeholder joint offset from the action and reports the two 3-vector end-effector positions; it loads no Isaac Sim or Isaac Lab, no PhysX scene, no Franka asset, beaker or table, and models no contacts, friction, gravity, actuators or sensors

one cap.world.step.v1 tick is one Matterix env.step (one control update), not one physics step: the default decimation is 5 and the default physics timestep is 1/60 s, so a tick advances 5/60 s = 83.33 ms while timestep_ms names the 1/60 s physics step (spec FID-015)
no wall-clock pacing: realtime_factor 0, the simulation advances only when step or reset is called
no physical device is modelled and nothing was validated against one; the README's real-world deployment claim has no hardware transport in this repository
the environment is vectorized upstream (num_envs defaults to 1); the fake serves one environment and its two spaces carry the batch dimension of one

the upstream environment needs Isaac Sim 5.0, Isaac Lab 3.0 and a cfg built by parse_env_cfg (README.md:39, scripts/random_agent.py:60-64); it could not be imported where the gate ran, so the fake was never compared with it
seeded determinism is claimed for the fake only; the upstream RNG and PhysX were not run and no trajectory comparison was made
snapshot and restore are not offered: MatterixBaseEnv defines no get_state or set_state method

measures.description: Last observation (derived from the observation space)
measures.name: observation

safe_state.description: the simulation stops advancing: the runtime latches the e-stop and no step or reset is accepted until mhs.safety.reset clears it; the last observation and tick stay readable
